newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court expects Iran trial verdict next week.
newsitem.headline: German court expects Iran trial verdict next week.

text.p: A Berlin court said on Thursday it planned to announce its verdict next week in the trial of five men accused of murdering three Iranian Kurdish dissidents and their translator in 1992.

The judges said they would announce the verdict next Thursday. The judgment in the marathon trial, which has lasted three and a half years so far, had been postponed several times to allow new evidence to be heard.
Prosecutors have blamed Iran for the gangland-style assassinations of the dissidents, who were gunned down while dining in Berlin's "Mykonos" restaurant.
The trial of four Lebanese and one Iranian has caused severe strains in ties between Bonn and Tehran.

Last year protesters marched on the German embassy in Tehran, pelted it with eggs and tomatoes, and called for the death of state prosecutor Bruno Jost after he accused Iran of ordering the assassinations.
Prosecutors have also issued an arrest warrant for Tehran's Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan in connection with the killings -- a move which also provoked fury in Iran.
Germany's anti-extremist watchdog, the Office for the Protection of the Constitution, has said it fears violence when the court issues its decision.

The latest target date for a verdict appeared in doubt earlier this week when one of the accused lodged an application to make a statement. But the judges said on Thursday he had now withdrawn his application.
